decision_rule.scope: Experimental heuristic, not a vendor standard or proof of unbounded queue growth
decision_rule.comparison: Per-node mean model waiting in final 100 seconds minus first 100 seconds; any increase above 2 fails this 300-second stage

direct_evidence.runtime: All MUSA workers V0 eager; standard MCCL with shared memory enabled, custom all-reduce disabled.

interpretation: Request-count round_robin equalizes counts but not the work of mixed lengths. Long output holds a running slot about one minute. Heavier worker(s) reach the configured 16-sequence cap while other replicas have spare sequence slots; waiting grows on .96. This demonstrates a queue boundary of the current configuration and allocation, not a whole-system hardware maximum.

secondary_observation.thermal_slowdown_stats: All recorded MUSA Thermal Slowdown Stats Count values were 0; both nodes reported P0.
secondary_observation.limitation: Clock difference is observed; its cause and causal contribution to queue growth are not established. The load generator shares .96; recorded benchmark CPU use was about 0.264 cores, insufficient evidence by itself for a CPU bottleneck.

reproduction.config: heterogeneous_compute/configs/system_benchmark.json and serving-snapshot.json in the run directory
reproduction.recipe: Select case 3 sent_at in [stage.start,stage.end). Join requests.request_id to routes.request_id and worker URL to frozen workers. Count mixed profiles by worker. Restrict telemetry received_at to the same stage; compute running-cap incidence, waiting, KV, preemption deltas and raw MUSA clocks/thermal counters.

maintenance: Retained useful diagnostic evidence and this summary. No experiment configuration, live services, limits or routing policy changed; no new model or SMI probes.
